This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 20.06.2019 passed by Additional MACT, Neemuch in Claim Case No.50/2017 seeking Rajendra Prakash Shyopura vs Bapulal Jat on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46541688/

sentences.text: The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the permanent disability suffered by the appellant, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,81,281/- along with interest.
The breakup of the compensation amount is as under:
HEAD AMOUNT

Medical Bills -Rs.1,37,656/-
 Repair of motorcycle -Rs.5,500/-

Attendant charges -Rs.7,500/-
 Conveyance -Rs.3,000/-
 Pain & suffering -Rs.20,000/-

Special diet -Rs.3,000/-
 Loss of income -Rs.69,625/-

Permanent disability -Rs.35,000/-
 --------------------

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The tribunal has committed an error in not applying the multiplier method while calculating the loss of income due to permanent disability.
The appellant has suffered 15% permanent disability.
He has suffered fracture in left hand radius ulna
boneAs per the income tax returns
the appellant was an income tax payee and his income shown in the income tax returns are Rs.27,000/- per month.
Hence, prays for awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.
As per the disability certificate Ex.P/17 the appellant/injured has suffered 60.32% permanent disablement in the left upper limb.
He remained in hospital for prolonged treatment.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the arguments advanced by the counsel for the parties and the evidence that came on record, in the considered opinion of this Court, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of permanent disability is on the lower side and the tribunal has committed an error in not applying the multiplier method for calculating the loss of income due to permanent disability.

Accordingly,
the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified as under:

 (i.e Rs.10000 25% FP=12500 x 12 x 15/100  PD x 14 (multiplier)
 Medical Bills -Rs.1,37,656/-
 Motorcycle repair -Rs.5,500/-

Special diet -Rs.3000/-

Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.5,61,281/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.2,81,281/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.2,80,000/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
8. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.2,80,000/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
